examples.en: The two singers sang a duet on stage.

examples.ko: 저와 친구는 노래방에서 듀엣 곡을 골랐어요.
examples.en: My friend and I picked a duet song at karaoke.

examples.ko: 이 듀엣의 목소리가 서로 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The voices of this duet go well together.

examples.ko: 듀엣으로 나온 두 사람이 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The two people who debuted as a duet became very popular.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 신부와 신랑이 듀엣을 할 거래요.
examples.en: I heard the bride and groom will do a duet at the wedding.
Timing together is important in a duet performance.

explain: '듀엣'은 두 사람이 함께 부르거나 연주하는 것, 또는 그 두 사람이에요. 세 명은 '트리오', 한 명은 '솔로'라고 해요. '듀엣을 하다/부르다'처럼 자연스럽게 말해요.

phrases.en: We sang a duet song at karaoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람이 함께 부르는 노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a song sung by two people together.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 듀엣 무대가 정말 멋졌어요.
phrases.en: The two people's duet performance was really great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연에서 둘이 함께 나오는 순서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a stage act where two perform together.

phrases.example: 그 노래는 듀엣으로 부르면 더 좋아요.
phrases.en: That song is better when sung as a duet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'를 붙여 둘이 함께 하는 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-(으)로' shows the way it is done, as two people.

explain_en: 듀엣 is two people singing or playing together, or the two people themselves. Three people is a 트리오 and one is a 솔로. It is natural to say 듀엣을 하다 or 듀엣을 부르다.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 멀티미디어 자료를 많이 써요.
examples.en: This class uses a lot of multimedia material.
The multimedia classroom has a big screen.
That company makes multimedia content.
Multimedia devices are very diverse these days.
I majored in multimedia at university.
I'm going to see a multimedia exhibition.

explain: 영상, 소리, 글을 함께 쓴 자료나 기술을 말해요. 일상 대화보다는 수업, 광고, 직업 이름 앞에서 '멀티미디어 교실', '멀티미디어 콘텐츠'처럼 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: This company makes multimedia content.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상, 소리, 글이 섞인 내용물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for content that mixes video, sound, and text.

phrases.en: I watch videos on a multimedia device.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상과 소리를 함께 쓰는 기계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for devices that handle both video and sound.

phrases.en: We watched a movie in the multimedia room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 도서관에서 영상 자료를 보는 방을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a room in a school or library for watching media.

explain_en: It refers to materials or technology that combine video, sound, and text. It appears less in casual talk and more as a modifier in school, ads, and job contexts, such as 멀티미디어 교실 or 멀티미디어 콘텐츠.

examples.en: This case is still a mystery.

examples.ko: 저는 밤에 미스터리 영화를 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I often watch mystery movies at night.
Solving a mystery is really fun.
There are a lot of mysteries on that island.
The mystery usually gets revealed at the end.
Mysteries are nice, but I like comedies more.

explain: '수수께끼'는 한국어 느낌이 나는 말이고 '미스터리'는 외래어예요. 장르를 말할 때는 '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'처럼 앞에 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I'm curious about the ending of mystery novels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장르 이름으로 '미스터리'를 앞에 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 'mystery' in front as a genre name.

phrases.en: This story is still a mystery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미스터리'와 비슷하지만 한국어 느낌이 나는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'mystery' but a native Korean word.

phrases.example: 미스터리한 이야기를 들으면 잠이 안 와요.
phrases.en: When I hear a mysterious story, I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미스터리한'으로 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Misteorihan' describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: '수수께끼' is the native Korean word and '미스터리' is a loanword. For genres, put it in front: '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'.

examples.en: When I go to a bookstore, I look at the new releases section first.
A new book by my favorite writer came out today.
I'll check whether new books have come into the library.

examples.ko: 이번 달 신간 중에서 하나를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked one from this month's new releases.

examples.ko: 신간은 보통 책값이 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: New books are usually a bit more expensive.
I gave my friend a newly published novel as a gift.

explain: 신간은 새로 나온 책이에요. 영화나 음악의 새 작품은 '신작'이라고 해서 책에만 써요. 서점에서는 오래전에 나온 책을 '구간'이라고도 하지만, 일상에서는 '예전에 나온 책'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Many new books arrived at the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서점이나 도서관 안내에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in bookstore and library notices.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 그 작가의 신간이 나와요.
phrases.en: That author's new book comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 책이 출판될 때 '나오다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 나오다 when a new book is published.

phrases.example: 이번 신간 소설을 꼭 사고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I really want to buy this new novel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 종류를 붙여 어떤 새 책인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the book type to say what kind of new release.

explain_en: 신간 is a newly published book. A new film or album is called '신작', so 신간 is used only for books. Bookstores sometimes call older titles '구간', but in daily speech people say '예전에 나온 책'.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 본명은 예명과 완전히 달라요.
examples.en: That singer's real name is completely different from the stage name.
I use a stage name when I sing.
The stage name is far more famous than the real name.
The singer performs under a stage name, so I don't know the real name.
I was curious what the stage name meant, so I looked up an interview.
Can I call you by your real name instead of your stage name?

explain: 가수나 배우가 활동할 때 쓰는 이름이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본명'이고, 글 쓰는 사람이 쓰는 이름은 '필명'이라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: The singer came up with the stage name herself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 활동 이름을 만들 때 '짓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 짓다 when someone creates a new name to perform under.
phrases.en_equiv: to come up with a stage name

phrases.en: That actor works under a stage name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본명 대신 다른 이름으로 일한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working under a different name instead of one's real name.
phrases.en_equiv: to work under a stage name

phrases.example: 그 가수의 본명은 많이 알려지지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That singer's real name isn't widely known.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예명과 짝이 되는 말로, 태어날 때 받은 진짜 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 예명: the real name a person was given at birth.

explain_en: It is the name a singer or actor uses while performing. Its counterpart is '본명' (real name), and the name a writer uses is called '필명' (pen name).

en: to be edited; to be compiled

examples.en: The video was edited nicely.
The interview is edited to fit the length.

examples.ko: 사진이 너무 많이 편집된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the photo has been edited too much.

examples.ko: 이 책은 여러 사람의 글이 모여 편집되었어요.
examples.en: This book was compiled from the writings of several people.
Unnecessary parts are cut out and the broadcast comes out.
When the file is edited, it is saved automatically.

explain: 영상·사진·글·책을 다듬고 정리해서 하나로 만든다는 뜻이에요. 글을 고치는 '수정하다'보다 전체 구성과 순서를 손보는 느낌이 강해요. 하는 사람은 '편집하다', 일을 하는 사람은 '편집자'예요.

phrases.en: This video is well edited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '편집'과 함께 결과가 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 편집 to say the editing turned out well.

phrases.en: My friend edited my video for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person doing the editing as the subject.

phrases.en: The editor read my writing and corrected it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편집하는 일을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person whose job is editing.

explain_en: It covers tidying and arranging video, photos, text or books into one finished piece. Compared with 수정하다 (fix), it feels more about the overall structure and order. The doer's verb is 편집하다 and the professional is a 편집자 (editor).

examples.en: This film is a joint work of Korea and France.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 두 가수의 합작품이라서 더 특별해요.
examples.en: That song is a collaboration of two singers, so it's more special.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 여러 건축가의 합작품으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: This building is known as the joint work of several architects.
The finished cake was a joint effort of the whole family.
For a joint work, the quality is really high.

examples.ko: 합작품은 의견을 맞추는 과정이 힘들 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a joint work, the process of matching opinions can be hard.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악처럼 두 나라나 두 사람 이상이 함께 만든 작품에 써요. 가볍게는 '우리 가족의 합작품'처럼 여럿이 힘을 모아 이룬 결과물에도 써요. '공동 작품'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 그림은 우리 반의 공동 작품이에요.
phrases.en: This painting is a joint work of our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합작품'을 풀어서 말한 표현이라 더 쉽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way of saying the headword, so it sounds easier.

phrases.example: 그 합작 영화는 두 나라에서 인기를 끌었어요.
phrases.en: That co-produced film was popular in both countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 나라 이상이 함께 만든 영화를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a film made together by two or more countries.

phrases.en: This cake is a joint effort of my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 힘을 모아 만든 결과물을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used lightly for something made by combining everyone's effort.

explain_en: It is used for works such as films, dramas and music made together by two countries or two or more people. In a lighter way, it also fits results many people made together, like '우리 가족의 합작품'. People sometimes say '공동 작품' instead.

examples.en: I rode the carousel at the amusement park.
The kids say they like the carousel best.
The carousel turns slowly, so it isn't scary.

examples.ko: 회전목마 앞에 줄이 길게 서 있어요.
examples.en: There is a long line in front of the carousel.

examples.ko: 회전목마에서 내리자마자 또 타고 싶다고 했어요.
examples.en: As soon as she got off the carousel, she said she wanted another ride.
At night the lights come on at the carousel and it looks pretty.

explain: 놀이공원에서 가장 순한 놀이기구를 말할 때 자주 나와요. 무서운 놀이기구는 '롤러코스터'나 '바이킹'이라고 하고, 회전목마는 어린아이도 탈 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I rode the carousel with my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이기구를 탄다고 할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you rode the attraction.

phrases.en: The carousel turns to the music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회전목마가 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the carousel in motion.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the carousel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이공원에서 만날 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for picking a meeting spot in an amusement park.

explain_en: 회전목마 comes up as the gentlest ride at an amusement park. Scary rides are called 롤러코스터 or 바이킹, while even small children can ride a 회전목마.
